measures.officialStatement: This amendment changes Article I, section 35 of the Tennessee Constitution by clarifying existing rights for crime victims and adding new rights.  The amendment gives victims new rights: to fair treatment; to be informed about and participate in the parole process; to be protected from harassment, intimidation, and abuse; to be informed of the minimum sentence the convicted criminal will serve, as well as their scheduled release date; and to have their safety, their family’s safety, and the public’s safety taken into account before any decision is made to release the convicted criminal.  The amendment also maintains or clarifies victims’ existing rights: to be informed about legal proceedings involving the accused or convicted criminal; to be present at public criminal proceedings; to be informed of any release, transfer, or escape of the accused or convicted criminal; to talk to prosecutors; to make statements about conviction, sentencing, or release of the accused person; to a speedy resolution of the case; to restitution from the convicted criminal; and to be informed of their rights.  The amendment does not restrict the powers of prosecutors or courts and does not create a cause of action or claim for damages against the State of Tennessee.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Revises crime victims’ rights in criminal and juvenile cases, including fair treatment; attendance at public proceedings; parole participation; protection from harassment; full and timely restitution; a speedy case outcome; and information about minimum sentences, scheduled release dates and victims’ rights. Victim, family and public safety must be considered before parole or other post-judgment release. On request, victims have rights to notice of proceedings, release, transfer or escape; to be heard in specified proceedings; and to consult prosecutors. Victims may assert their rights through procedures set by the legislature, without becoming parties to the case. Due-process rights and prosecutors’ and courts’ powers are preserved. These rights do not permit overturning a conviction or create a damages claim against the state, local governments, their personnel or court personnel.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Replace the current constitutional crime-victim rights section with the revised provisions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Keep the current constitutional crime-victim rights section.
